title: Runbook provenance archiver with safe-recall and signed checkpoints
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: On-call runbooks and automated playbooks are frequently edited during incidents; teams need an auditable, compact archive that preserves runbook provenance, safe recall of executable steps, and cryptographic proof that a particular archived snapshot was used in a remediation. This PR introduces a Runbook Provenance Archiver service and CLI that creates signed checkpoints, stores compact telemetry-aligned snapshots, and provides a safe-recall API for oncall UIs to replay a runbook state without executing any live actions.

What this changes: Adds a lightweight archiver that captures runbook content, associated telemetry snapshot pointers, who triggered the archive, and a signing envelope (RSA/ECDSA) to prove authorship/time. The archive format is gzip'd JSON with an embedded manifest and optional compact trace pointer (trace id + window). A safe-recall endpoint (read-only) reconstructs a display-ready ephemeral runbook with metadata and a non-executable annotation layer that flags auto-remediation hooks as inert.

Design notes: The archiver is intentionally decoupled from persistent incident storage. It writes objects to the existing telemetry blobstore using a deterministic key derived from the checkpoint hash and signer key id. Signed checkpoints include: checkpoint_id, archived_by, linear_refs (Linear ticket ids), telemetry_snapshot_ref, checksum, signer_id, signature, created_at. The service exposes a POST /v1/archives endpoint (authenticated via existing SSO tokens) and a GET /v1/archives/:id?replay=true for safe-recall.

Security & safety: Archives are read-only and stored with ACLs; the safe-recall response contains explicit non-executable markers for any remediation steps. An additional sec-scan validates that no secrets are included before committing an archive; the CLI runs a lightweight sanitizer that strips patterns matching credential patterns and redacts known PII keys. Signing uses the platform crypto abstraction so HSM-backed keys in private deployments are supported.

Testing & rollout: Unit tests for serializer, signer, and replay were added. An e2e test simulates creating an archive during a synthetic incident and verifying replay is inert. Feature flagged behind slo_archiver.enabled; rollout plan: enable for 5% of teams, monitor archive size and safe-recall latency for two weeks, then expand.

Migration & rollback: No DB migrations. Rolling back disables the feature flag and purges archived objects created during the rollout window if requested by SRE compliance.

Checklist:
- [x] Archiver service & API
- [x] CLI for local archiving and inspection
- [x] Signed checkpoint format and signer integration
- [x] Sanitizer for secrets/PII
- [x] Documentation and runbook for operators
- [x] Unit and e2e tests

Notes: This PR is self-contained and avoids touching runbook execution paths; the goal is auditability and safe replaying, not automation. Related: ENG-8421 (oncall auditability), SRE-127 (incident forensics improvements).

review_comments: Sofia Patel (review): Can we guarantee that the sanitizer pattern list is configurable per-tenant? Some tenants have custom keys.
Maya Chen (author): The sanitizer uses a base list plus tenant-override file under /etc/archiver/sanitize.d; documented in operator guide.
Ethan Brooks (review): Suggest using short-lived replay tokens rather than raw archive object IDs in the UI to avoid accidental link sharing.
Maya Chen (author): Added replay-token issuance step and example TTL=15m in the API contract; updated tests.
Liam Gomez (review): Security scan flagged a use of standard crypto RNG during key id generation; prefer platform-crypto RNG.
Maya Chen (author): Switched to platform-crypto RNG; re-ran sec-scan and it passes.
release_notes: Adds a Runbook Provenance Archiver: teams can create cryptographically-signed archives of runbooks and aligned telemetry snapshots for auditability and safe replay. Includes CLI, API, and operator docs. Backward compatible and feature-flagged.
